extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and trainee news reporters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplar news stories illustrating how to report fires, accidents, and disasters — what facts to include, how to structure the account, and pedagogical prompts (e.g., comparing different paper's treatments of the same event).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescue-response details
rubrics_metrics.description: Report who responded to the emergency and what they did (numbers and roles of surgeons, nurses, emergency men, firemen, police reserves, ambulance doctors, officials who arrived and directed work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give numbers, titles and actions (e.g., 'a force of thirty surgeons and as many more nurses', 'fifty additional firemen without apparatus were called out'). Identify who directed rescue operations (Fire Chief, Acting Chief Inspector) and note organization of the effort and timing (arrived early, called from all parts of Manhattan and the Bronx).

rubrics_metrics.name: Casualty identification and particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Name deceased and injured persons and where available include address, occupation, age and immediate outcome (died on scene, died after removal, taken to hospital).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific identifiers as in examples ('Louis Krugman, a garment worker, of 308 East Eighth Street'), and list of dead/injured compiled from hospitals. Be precise about status (dead, wounded, treated in streets, expected to die).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical treatment and triage information
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how and where the injured were treated, who received first aid, and which hospitals received the worst injured or the majority of casualties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note on-scene care (treated in the streets by ambulance doctors), hospital destinations (emergency hospital of the Suit Company, St. Vincent's) and special actions (anointing, refusal of stimulants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazards, utilities and technical damage
rubrics_metrics.description: Report broken utilities, immediate hazards (gas odor, broken water mains), and the technical steps taken to mitigate hazards (shutting off mains, installing temporary services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specifics like sizes/types of mains broken (e.g., 'one twenty-four-inch high pressure fire main and several six-inch water mains'), times to response ('employes at the cavity in eight minutes'), and measures taken to restore service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official quotes and eyewitness attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quotations from officials or eyewitnesses to convey evaluation, opinion, and salient judgments about the event and its causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include attributed quotes to illustrate perspective (e.g., Colonel William Hayward's remarks about wooden vs steel cars) and make clear the speaker's role and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual background (contracts, companies, liabilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide background about parties involved (contractors, companies), financial and contractual details, and legal/insurance context relevant to the accident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give contract values, percent complete, bonds, corporate assets and lists of company officers when relevant to likely litigation or public interest (examples list contract price, percent complete, bond and officers of the United States Realty and Improvement Company). Note statutory liability (workmen's compensation) and insurance status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational impact and service disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Report effects on public services and normal operations (suspension of transit service, blocked rail lines, traffic disruptions) and expected timelines for resumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State geographic scope and estimated duration (e.g., 'Seventh Avenue car service was suspended south of Thirty-second Street... at least a week before service is resumed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause and mechanical/technical explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: When available, report mechanical causes or proximate technical failures (broken wheel tire, broken rail, open switch) and relevant findings of investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite investigative findings plainly ('the police... found a broken rail... agreed that this was the cause') or reported mechanical failures ('the tire on one of the rear drive-wheels came off').

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest and scene detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Include humanizing details and sensory description to convey the scene and stakes (stifling odor of gas, fetid hold, spectators' alarm, personal circumstances like 'would have entered high school').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, vivid details that illuminate human cost and atmosphere without distracting from facts (examples throughout accounts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety lessons and evaluative commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Report lessons learned or expert/official evaluations about safety (e.g., design choices that affected survivability such as wooden vs steel cars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute evaluative statements to named authorities and show implications (Hayward's assertion that 'If that car had been a steel car I do not believe a person would have been hurt').

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics of rescue and salvage operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe management of salvage and rescue: who supervised, special equipment used (derricks, wreckers), timing, and complications (alarm boxes out of commission, wrecker arrival times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give sequence and duration of operations where relevant (e.g., wrecker took over two hours to get the engine on the rails) and name responsible officers or companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative and legal follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Note arrests, coroner's inquests, official investigations and statements about responsibility or the absence thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report arrests and their immediate judicial outcome (e.g., superintendent remanded to coroner), coroner's inquiries, and ongoing investigations by police or federal inspectors when mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Victim and hospital lists as factual roll-call
rubrics_metrics.description: When many are injured, publish compiled lists of injured with brief condition/status drawn from hospitals and morgues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names, ages, home towns and brief injury description as compiled by hospitals (as in the long list from the Jersey City wreck).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative analysis of different accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: As a teaching device, compare how two papers report the same accident to show differences of angle, emphasis, detail and tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly instructs: 'Note — The following two stories should be compared as reports of the same accident given in two New York morning papers.' Use side-by-side comparison to highlight choices reporters made (detail selection, moralizing, technical emphasis, human-interest angle).
